stale_prose_tests.fixed_prose_before: Natural selection preserves favorable variations and rejects injurious ones, while neutral variations remain fluctuating elements in populations, especially under changing environmental conditions such as climate shifts. Selection operators in the DEAP evolutionary computation framework select individuals from a population based on criteria like fitness, without duplicating individuals during the selection process. Common selection methods implemented in DEAP include random selection, best and worst selection, tournament selection, roulette wheel selection, and double tournament selection, each with specific mechanisms and use cases. Double tournament selection in DEAP uses both fitness and individual size to reduce bloat in genetic programming, with parameters controlling tournament sizes and order, as described in Luke and Panait (2002).
